narr: A highly anomalous weather pattern involving a closed low and a trailing cold front brought discrete thunderstorms and multicell clusters in multiple rounds to east Tennessee. Repeat events as well as training of cells resulted in flash flooding, some of it significant.
ev: Floodwaters blocked Emory Road near the community of Blaine.
Flooding of grounds in a residential neighborhood of Englewood.
Rainbrook Lane was washed out near the community of Limestone.
Flood waters covered several roads from a few inches deep up to impassable depths. Includes County Roads 197 and 436, northwest and east of Athens, respectively.
Several roadways around White Pine were impassable due to flooding, including School Street. One retaining wall reported to have collapsed.

Multiple road closures due to flash flooding. Washouts occurred along the Cherohala Skyway at MM 4.5, and along Hwy 360 northeast of Tellico Plains. Other road damages in the Cherokee National Forest blocked access to homes. Floodwaters entered several buildings, and flooded the ball park to nearly a foot of depth. Rain gauge and radar estimates depicted around 5 inches of rain fell over this mountainous area. EM estimates $6 million in damages to the area, while another $4 million was requested for repairs in the National Forest. These estimates did not include apparent losses to agriculture.
